Here's the complete list of Brazilian Ministers of Agriculture (Ministro da Agricultura e Pecuária / MAPA) from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024:

---

## 🌾 Ministers of Agriculture & Livestock (Brazil), 2018–2024

### 1. **Blairo Maggi** *(Progressistas / PP)*
- **In office:** January 1, 2018 – January 1, 2019
- **Presidency:** Michel Temer (post-Dilma Rousseff impeachment)
- He began his tenure much earlier (May 2016, under Temer), but he served through the entirety of 2018 before transitioning to Jair Bolsonaro's government.

---

### 2. **Tereza Cristina** *(DEM → PL)*
- **In office:** January 1, 2019 – March 30, 2022
- **Presidency:** Jair Bolsonaro
- First woman to lead Brazil's agriculture ministry; served for nearly three years.

---

### 3. **Marcos Montes** *(PSD – Social Democratic Party)*
- **In office:** March 30, 2022 – January 1, 2023
- **Presidency:** Jair Bolsonaro (second term)
- Ex-mayor of Uberaba, MG; had a relatively short tenure, succeeding Tereza Cristina during Bolsonaro's re-election aftermath.

---

### 4. **Carlos Fávaro** *(PSD – Social Democratic Party)*
- **In office:** January 1, 2023 – present (still serving as of December 2024)
- **Presidency:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
- Took over directly from Marcos Montes with no gap in service; remains the incumbent minister as of end of 2024.

---

### Timeline Summary

| Minister | Party | Period Covered | President |
|----------|-------|---------------|-----------|
| Blairo Maggi | PP | Jan 2018 – Dec 2018 | Michel Temer |
| Tereza Cristina | DEM (now PL) | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022 | Jair Bolsonaro |
| Marcos Montes | PSD | Mar 2022 – Dec 2022 | Jair Bolsonaro |
| Carlos Fávaro | PSD | Jan 2023 – Dec 2024 | Lula da Silva |

---

**Note:** The ministry was formally called *Ministério da Agricultura, Pecuária e Abastecimento* (MAPA) until March 2023, when it was renamed *Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária* under Lula's government. No interim replacements occurred during this period — each transition happened via an official handover ceremony without gaps in leadership.

# Ministry of Agriculture (Brazil)

Federal ministry of Brazil

*Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock*

| [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária* | |
| --- | --- |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/MAPAAssinatura.png/250px-MAPAAssinatura.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MAPAAssinatura.png) | |
| Ministry overview | |
| Formed | 2 March 1861; 165 years ago (1861-03-02) |
| Type | [Ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_(government_department) "Ministry (government department)") |
| Jurisdiction | [Federal government of Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") |
| Headquarters | [Esplanada dos Ministérios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monumental_Axis "Monumental Axis"), Bloco D   [Brasília](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasília "Brasília"), [Federal District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_District_(Brazil) "Federal District (Brazil)") |
| Annual budget | $9.97 b [BRL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_real "Brazilian real") (2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-1) |
| Ministry executives | [Carlos Fávaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Fávaro "Carlos Fávaro"), MinisterIrajá Rezende, Executive-SecretaryNeri Geller, Secretary of Agricultural PolicyCarlos Goulart, Secretary of Agricultural DefenseRenata Miranda, Secretary of Innovation, Sustainable Development, Irrigation and CooperativismRoberto Perosa, Secretary of Trade and Foreign AffairsNaur Pontes, Director of the [National Institute of Meteorology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Meteorology "National Institute of Meteorology") |
| Website | [www.gov.br/agricultura/](https://www.gov.br/agricultura/) |

The **Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária*, abbreviated **MAPA**) is a [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") department in Brazil. The jurisdiction of this ministry is to formulate and implement policies for [agribusiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agribusiness "Agribusiness") development, integrating the aspects of market, technological, organizational and environmental care for the consumers of the country and abroad, promoting [food security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security "Food security"), income generation and employment, reducing inequalities and increasing social inclusion.

The Ministry was founded during the [Brazilian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Empire "Brazilian Empire") in 1860. Originally named *Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas*, the body was extinguished in the early years of the [First Brazilian Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Brazilian_Republic "First Brazilian Republic") and re-established in 1906 as the *Ministerio dos Negocios da Agricultura, Industria e Commercio*.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-2) In 1930, it was renamed the *Ministério da Agricultura*.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-3) From 2001–2022 it was the *Ministério da Agricultura, Pecuária e Abastecimento*, from which the acronym MAPA derives.

## Agroenergy

Brazil is the world leader in producing agroenergy and the Ministry of Agriculture encourages policies which develop [ethanol fuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol_fuel "Ethanol fuel") production.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-4)
